primary_antecedent.author: Lars Hörmander
primary_antecedent.title: The Analysis of Linear Partial Differential Operators III: Pseudo-Differential Operators
primary_antecedent.edition: Springer 2007, reprint of the corrected 1994 edition
primary_antecedent.locator: Sections 18.3 and 24.7; Propositions 24.7.1 and 24.7.1-prime, printed pages 465–467.
primary_antecedent.receiving_contribution: Independent exact scalar assembly across arbitrary compact microlocal patches in a positive-dimensional boundary chart, using orthogonal relocation only of full residual outputs.

source_correspondence: H0–H1 specify arbitrary bounded full-kernel families, common compact projections and compact uniform microsupport in the prescribed cone. They impose no whole-input product-cone condition. The dimension and boundary-chart scope are explicit.

E0 uses one fixed full microlocal inverse to give an exact order-zero factor and a bounded complete residual family. The proof uses continuity of full-kernel operations, so auxiliary indices need no smooth extension.

E1 invokes the exact scalar residual Fourier factorization with its actual logarithmic half-density, compact inverse Fourier kernel and bounded quotient operators. Its residual theorem has no product-cone restriction.

R0 proves the tangential affine isometry and its inverse by the exact Jacobian. The normal and input coordinates are unchanged. The fixed relocated output projection is separated from the elliptic output.

R1 proves membership of the whole relocated kernel in the residual boundary class: all resolved normal coordinates, every derivative, both flat side faces and compact projections are retained. Only residual kernels are moved.

R2 proves exact orthogonality, smooth extraction of both output channels, and an actual bounded right factorization of every original operator. The finite norm constant is retained and can be absorbed into the scalar test.

C0 checks full input support, microsupport, finite matrix fibers and geometric choices independent of the target order. It does not infer arbitrary compact-manifold or zero-dimensional-boundary assembly from the chart construction.

C1 independently assembles the complete source and observation lists of actual local estimates. It permits varying equation inputs and arbitrary bounded auxiliary indices, and keeps propagation to the final observation cone as a separate obligation.

C2 applies the assembler to the full boundary-regularization source tree, giving one scalar order-zero source test for the actual ordinary H2 graph, equation and both traces without a whole-input source rectangle.
C3 proves injectivity and actual distributional actions for the completed tested graphs using flat transposed kernels. It does not presume a graph-density theorem.
Three complete solutions verify the affine map, density and every displayed derivative factor, the sharp numerical norm constant and a two-patch configuration that fails the older product condition.
The proof map identifies the exact earlier programme prerequisites. Linked human components retain their authorship and licence notices.
